A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same polysemantic-intervention study despite the changed title and expanded scope. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison; revised experimental settings require caution when comparing scores.

before.justification: V1 reports original feature-, token-, prompt-, and neuron-intervention experiments, including transfer results and appendix replications.

after.justification: V2 reports original intervention results, additional transfer evaluations, HellaSwag experiments, and feature-pair annotation and comparison analyses.

M1.justification: The four intervention mechanisms and their SAE/gradient constructions remain. However, v2 Appendices K.1–K.2 construct transferred token pools using the union of tokens from the two small models, whereas v1 Section 3.4 and Appendix H.2 use their intersection. This changes transfer-input selection.

E1.justification: V2 expands systematic prompt-injection evaluation beyond v1's location and hate/love tables to eight categories, including numbers, science, animals, colors, and time. It also adds HellaSwag commonsense-completion evaluation and feature-pair association judgments, substantially broadening the tested tasks and scenarios.

E2.justification: The random, target-feature/token, and interference-level controls remain, as does comparison between SAE-direction and gradient steering, although their displays change. Added language models serve as intervention targets or analysis annotators; no new competing intervention method is evaluated.

E3.justification: V2 replaces top-10, four-metric evaluation with full-distribution cosine/overlap measures and relative changes; prompt success changes from top-10 to top-30. Semantic cutoffs change from 0.5 to four thresholds between 0.40 and 0.15, with revised sampling and interference bins. V2 adds Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct, matched-pair judgments, and 500 HellaSwag items tested with 174 vectors at quarter strength. Appendix I.2's positive scaling grid conflicts with the retained [-20,20] description.

E4.justification: V2 adds semantic-threshold sensitivity tests, controlled regressions, semantic/interference distributions, alternative DeepSeek-V3 feature interpretations, HellaSwag collateral-performance checks, and hidden-association analyses. These test substantial new robustness and explanatory questions. V1's independent feature/token/neuron replication panels and supplementary prompt-metric plots are no longer reported.

E5.justification: V1's standard-error displays are replaced by 95% confidence intervals, with regression estimates also showing 90% and 99% intervals. Prompt-table significance changes from z-tests to t-tests. New association analyses report Wilson intervals, an exact binomial test, and annotator agreement including Cohen's kappa. The stated 100 injection samples per prompt remain unchanged; these additions do not establish more repeated runs.

E6.justification: Numerous results are replaced or added. Llama-3.1-8B location high-interference success changes from 27.64% in v1 Table 2 to 20.78% in v2 Table 1 under different protocols, so this is not a directly comparable decline. V2 adds mixed transfer outcomes across categories and 70B results, HellaSwag's reported 2.77% average accuracy reduction from a 77.2% baseline, and association findings of 27.7% related pairs and 64.3% matched-choice preference.

T1.justification: V2 substantively revises the mathematical evaluation definitions to use full output distributions and relative effects, including an epsilon-stabilized relative-overlap formula. The Kendall and Spearman criteria disappear. The SAE equations, transported steering-vector formulation, and token-gradient derivation remain unchanged after relocation; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The intervention, transfer, and super-neuron claims remain, but v2 makes unexplained, counterintuitive shared structure a central contribution. Its abstract, introduction, and conclusion now emphasize that most annotated interference pairs lack recognized higher-order associations and may generate hypotheses about latent knowledge. The transfer claim also explicitly extends to 70B models.

C2.justification: V2 develops v1's open question about higher-order organization into substantive interpretations involving semantic priming, morphology, and latent knowledge. Section 3.5 adds the Beethoven/frustration hypothesis and proposes human validation. Appendices K–L identify categories without strong generalizability and acknowledge potential performance damage motivating weaker steering. The principal SAE-dependence and single-layer limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 identifies text-embedding-3-large, expands token-classification and sentence-generation instructions, details token-pool filtering and deduplication, lists a scaling grid, and supplies annotation prompts and matching tolerances. These substantially expand reproducibility information. Hardware/timing disclosures largely persist; both PDFs advertise the same repository and withholding of shared-direction matrices, so the separate reproducibility statement does not establish a new release.

R1.justification: V2 adds semantic-priming and morphology connections through Mandera and Bojanowski, supporting SAE and threshold-selection citations, and replaces v1's unresolved Appendix A.2 citation. Existing related-work organization and the challenge to incidental-polysemanticity explanations largely remain. Novelty wording strengthens from 'among the first' to 'the first.'

P1.justification: The title and abstract are rewritten, and the research questions, evaluation exposition, and discussion are substantially recast. The main-text dataset subsection and boxed Finding summaries disappear, while appendices are reorganized into dedicated methodological, analysis, and disclosure sections. James Evans is added as an author.

P2.justification: Figures 3–4 replace four-metric panels with threshold-grouped bars and regression plots; Figure 5 changes from bars to distribution boxplots. V1 Table 1 moves to v2 Appendix Table 3, and the two neuron-distribution figures merge. New figures and tables display semantic distributions, interpreter comparisons, annotations, HellaSwag examples, and expanded prompt results; original replication grids disappear.

improvement.justification: V2 directly addresses v1's weak validation of semantic distinctness through stricter threshold sweeps, controlled regressions, and alternative feature interpretations, substantially strengthening evidence for the central interference finding. HellaSwag and weak-transfer categories add meaningful evidence about costs and boundaries. These gains outweigh the removed replication panels, although conclusions about human cognition remain indirect and Appendix K's union construction is insufficiently reconciled with claims about shared transfer tokens.
